color.note: Colors are designed in OKLCH: the same role sits in the same lightness band, the hue stays fixed, and chroma goes only as high as the sRGB gamut allows. Neutrals share one hue (h 286, a touch of blue); transparent lines and fills are alpha of black or white. Contrast ratios are in the notes and are remeasured when a value changes.

tokens.name: bg
tokens.usage: Page background. Cards sit on top of it; pure black in the dark theme.

tokens.name: surface
tokens.usage: Fill of a focused field (input :focus) and the base of the tooltip glass.

tokens.name: card
tokens.usage: Card panel and Stat surface. Very close to the background in the dark theme; a gradient border (gradientBorder-*) separates them, not a shadow.

tokens.name: surface-2
tokens.usage: Opaque secondary surface: the base of the color mix in heatmap cells (color-mix(..., var(--surface-2))).

tokens.name: text

tokens.name: text-2

tokens.name: muted

tokens.name: hairline

tokens.name: fill

scale.note: Type scale: component CSS reads font-size only from here (var(--fs-*)); no px, rem or half pixels (em only on elements sized relative to their text) (npm run typecheck › scripts/font-sizes.mjs). 1px steps at the small end (a dense interface lives between 11 and 15px), about a 1.2 ratio at the large end. If you need a one-off size, try the nearest step first; if that doesn't work, add it to the scale with a reason.

skin.note: Materials (data-skin) are not color themes; they're the language of the surface: highlight lines, shadows, knobs, recesses. Set one on any element (regional); the nearest data-skin wins, and data-skin='mizan' returns to the default. Light and dark themes work in every material through color-scheme. Variables derived with var() at the root (derived) are rewritten in every material block, so a regional material doesn't inherit the old value already resolved at the root.

defaults.control: linear-gradient(180deg, var(--control-top), var(--control-bottom) 72%, color-mix(in oklab, var(--control-bottom) 55%, var(--control-top)))

bevel.note: bevel: a beveled-edge language (adapted from hazeglow.dev). In light, a milk-white page and milk-toned surfaces (warm, single hue h 85; no blue); in dark, a black page and cool gray surfaces (h 230). Raised controls get a highlight on top, a shadow line below and a 1px border; inset controls get an inner shadow; metal knobs. Text uses the same cool hue (h 230); contrasts are in each token's note.
